land.text: Algiers and nearby coastal points, entered by French troops on 5 July 1830

predecessors.note: The French Algeria page lists the Regency of Algiers first among its predecessors, with the Emirate of Abdelkader, the Kingdom of Beni Abbas and the Kel Ahaggar; only Algiers and its surroundings pass at the birth (a 30 km radius: the Cliopatria 1830 shape runs west from Sidi Ferruch to Miliana's longitude and misses the city, see the first keyframe). The later gains come from the Regency's remnant lands, the Emirate and the Beylik of Constantine (see the ledger).

land.text: Algeria as Cliopatria's French Africa row draws it from 1848, the year the Second Republic's constitution declared Algeria an integral part of France with three departments

successors.note: The French Algeria page runs the colony 1830-1848 and 'part of France' 1848-1962. Cliopatria ends its French Algeria row in 1847 and its French Africa row takes the same land (799 cells) in 1848. The Algerian land after 1848 is the french-africa dossier's (another group), not this one.

capitals.name: Algiers
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital and largest city: Algiers'. Abd al-Qadir's rival capitals (Mascara, Tagdemt) belong to the emirate-of-abdelkader dossier.

correction.text: Algiers and nearby coastal points, the page's words: a 30 km radius round Algiers (the city, the Sidi Ferruch landing coast and the Sahel), without the Cliopatria shape's inland cells to Miliana and without its Oran and Bône cells

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1830 shape is 4,234 km2 (15 cells): ten cells from Sidi Ferruch (2.85 E) west to 2.03 E and 36.3 N, which reach Miliana (occupied only in 1840, Miliana page) and miss the city of Algiers (3.06 E), four cells at Oran and one at Bône. The conquest page puts French control in 1830 at Algiers and nearby coastal points: Clauzel's November 1830 column occupied Médéa and left 500 men at Blida, the French lost both, and 'France was only able to capture Blida in 1839'; Bourmont had sent troops to occupy Bône and Oran and withdrew them after the July revolution; Rovigo (appointed at the end of 1831) 'regained control of Bône and Bougie'; Voirol 'established French occupation in Oran' in 1833. The correction is therefore a 30 km radius round Algiers (6 cells, about 1,500 km2), and Bône (1832) and Oran (1833) enter by the ledger. Unverified: the pages do not narrate what garrisons stood at Oran and Bône in 1830-1831, which Cliopatria draws; the cells are dropped on the pages' dates, not on a page that denies a garrison. No infobox area for 1830 (the page gives 585,814 km2 for 1899 only). Years cut to 1830-1831 because Bône is regained in 1832.

correction.text: Algiers and nearby coastal points, plus Bône (Annaba), regained by Rovigo

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the conquest page has Rovigo, appointed at the end of 1831, 'regained control of Bône and Bougie' that Clauzel had taken and lost; the Annaba page dates the French occupation of the city to 1832 ('Rule by the Ottoman Empire began in 1533, and that lasted until French occupation in 1832'). Cliopatria draws a Bône cell from 1830. Bougie is retaken in 1833 on the conquest page.

correction.text: Algiers, Bône, Bougie (Béjaïa) and the coast around Oran, Arzew and Mostaganem

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the conquest page has Bougie captured in 1833 (the city 'from Kabyle and Kouloughli forces') and, in the same section, Voirol establishing French occupation in Oran and Desmichels gaining control of Arzew and Mostaganem. Cliopatria adds Bougie only in 1834 and never draws Arzew and Mostaganem before 1842.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1834 shape for 1834-1836 without Kabylia, Bouira, Blida and Miliana's province: the 'area of limited occupation near the coast' (Algiers and the Sahel, the coastal Mitidja, Bône, Bougie, Oran, Arzew and Mostaganem)

keyframe_review.note: 15,320 km2 (55 cells), but its Algiers part grows from 1.91-3.00 E (2,806 km2 in 1830) to 1.91-5.41 E and 36.22-36.93 N (13,887 km2): the added cells are Blida (9 of 9 cells), Boumerdès, Bouira (8), Tizi Ouzou (10 of 10) and the Béjaïa interior (12), none in the 1830 shape, and the ledger had no gain to explain them. The conquest page: 'On 22 June 1834, France formally annexed the occupied areas' with authority 'nominally over an area of "limited occupation" near the coast'; the Hadjout were attacked in 1834 and 'crushed by August 1835'; the French reached Larbaa on 24-26 February 1837; 'France was only able to capture Blida in 1839'. The French Algeria page has Kabylia as the only region independent of the French government. The correction (about 41 cells, 10,400 km2) removes Kabylia, Bouira, Blida and Aïn Defla (Miliana, occupied in 1840) and adds back a 30 km radius round Algiers, Bône, Bougie, Oran and Mostaganem. The Tipaza and Boumerdès cells that remain (Sahel, coastal Mitidja to the Isser) are Cliopatria's: no page dates them beyond the annexation and the Hadjout campaign (ledger 1834, confidence 1). Kabylia stays out of every keyframe: the Kabylia page has 'Kabylia as a whole' fully conquered only in 1857 (Battle of Icheriden), and the French Algeria page has Kabylia as the only region independent of the French government. The region is Tizi Ouzou and Béjaïa provinces (48 cells) and Bouira province; Bougie's own radius is added back. The Desmichels treaty of 26 February 1834 left the Oran interior to Abd al-Qadir (Emirate page).

correction.text: the 1834 correction plus Constantine, stormed on 13 October 1837

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the French Algeria page has Valée capturing Constantine on 13 October 1837 (Clauzel was repulsed there in November 1836); Cliopatria draws the Constantine country only from 1840. The Tafna treaty of 30 May 1837 left the emir 'about two thirds of Algeria' (Tafna page), so the Algiers part does not grow.

correction.text: the 1837 shape plus Blida and its province, captured in 1839

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'France was only able to capture Blida in 1839' (conquest page, after the 1830 battles of Blida); the Mitidja campaign of 1839 ended at Oued El Alleug and the Iron Gates were passed in late 1839. Cliopatria draws Blida from 1834.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1840 shape (the Algiers-Constantine belt, with Miliana's province) without Kabylia and Bouira, plus the 30 km radii of Algiers, Bône, Bougie, Oran, Mostaganem and Constantine

keyframe_review.note: 29,467 km2: the shape adds the belt from Bougie through Sétif and Constantine to Philippeville and Bône, and Miliana's province (Aïn Defla). The conquest page: the policy of 'limited occupation' was 'formally abandoned in 1840 for one of complete control'; the French marched through the Iron Gates in late 1839; the Miliana page: 'The city was occupied in 1840 by Marshal Valée's troops, but the garrison was sieged several times'. The belt's cells are Cliopatria's, the year the pages'. Kabylia and Bouira are subtracted as in 1834: the march through the Iron Gates, which cross the Bouira-Bordj Bou Arréridj edge, took no ground the pages date. Médéa is not in the shape: the Médéa and conquest pages give no French date for it. Kabylia stays out of every keyframe: the Kabylia page has 'Kabylia as a whole' fully conquered only in 1857 (Battle of Icheriden), and the French Algeria page has Kabylia as the only region independent of the French government. The region is Tizi Ouzou and Béjaïa provinces (48 cells) and Bouira province; Bougie's own radius is added back.

correction.text: the 1840 shape plus Mascara, where 'the French establish full control' in 1841

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Mascara page's timeline has '1841: The French establish full control over Mascara' (it had been destroyed by the French in 1835). The cells are the Mascara part of Cliopatria's 1842 shape (12 of the province's cells). Cliopatria draws Mascara from 1842.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1842 shape for 1842-1843 (the Oran-Tlemcen-Mascara block added to the 1840 belt) without Kabylia and Bouira, plus the radii of Algiers, Bône, Bougie, Oran, Mostaganem and Constantine

keyframe_review.note: 48,573 km2: the shape adds a 76-cell block from Oran south to Tlemcen and Mascara, west to -1.99 E. The Tlemcen page's timeline has 'France, (French Algeria) 1842-1962' for Tlemcen (Clauzel had entered the city in 1836 'deserted by the Moors'); the Mascara page has full French control in 1841; the Miliana page has Miliana 'under French control in 1842'; the conquest page has Abd al-Qadir 'driven into Morocco in 1842'. The block is therefore dated at the year level (Mascara 1841, Tlemcen and Miliana 1842); its extents are Cliopatria's. Kabylia stays out of every keyframe: the Kabylia page has 'Kabylia as a whole' fully conquered only in 1857 (Battle of Icheriden), and the French Algeria page has Kabylia as the only region independent of the French government. The region is Tizi Ouzou and Béjaïa provinces (48 cells) and Bouira province; Bougie's own radius is added back. Cut to 1842-1843 because Biskra is added in 1844.

correction.text: the 1842 shape plus Biskra, where the Saharan expedition began in March 1844

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the conquest page has the Saharan expedition beginning at Biskra under the Duke of Aumale in March 1844; Cliopatria draws Biskra only in 1846. The smala was raided in 1843 and the Treaty of Tangier (10 September 1844) and the Treaty of Lalla Maghnia (18 March 1845, First Franco-Moroccan War page) fix the western edge, which the shape already has at -1.99 E.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1846 shape for 1846-1847 without Kabylia, Bouira and the two cells in modern Tunisia, plus the 1842 and 1844 shapes' own cells and the radii of Algiers, Bône, Bougie, Oran, Mostaganem, Constantine and Biskra

keyframe_review.note: 211,876 km2 (the area column; 801 land cells, 2 of them in modern Tunisia at 8.4 E, about 500 km2): a fourfold jump from 1845 that takes in the Tell, the High Plateaux and the Ziban to 33.6 N and the whole east to the Tunisian edge. After the correction about 770 cells (195,000 km2). The conquest page dates only steps: the smala raid (1843), Biskra (March 1844), the Kabylia campaign of 1845, the ambush at Issers and the surrender of Ahmed bin Salem in 1846 (which the page says ended Abd al-Qadir's influence in the east), and the surrender of Abd al-Qadir in December 1847; it gives no extent of French control in 1846. Kabylia is subtracted as in 1834 (the 1845 Battle of Tizi Ouzou and the 1846 Issers ambush are battles at its edge, not control; Kabylia page: conquered in 1857). Bouira province is subtracted whole, which also removes the Aumale country in its south: no page opened dates it. The southern edge is the page's silence: the shape's lowest cells (33.56 N) lie in Djelfa province and it does not contain Laghouat province, and the Laghouat page dates the French taking of Laghouat to the siege of 21 November-4 December 1852, so the edge is not contradicted by it. The Médéa page gives no French date for Médéa (it was one of the emir's capitals after Tafna, 1837), and the Miliana page has Miliana under French control in 1842, so the Médéa province (33 cells) is the shape's, unverified. The shape is 36 per cent of the infobox's only area before 1962 (585,814 km2 for 1899, after the Kabylia and Saharan conquests), so the two are not comparable. The two Tunisian cells are subtracted: the pages place the Beylik of Tunis to the east and no French claim there, and the 1846 frontier was undelimited.

region.text: Algiers and nearby coastal points

ledger.note: 5 July 1830: French troops enter Algiers and the dey capitulates. Infobox 'Established: Surrender of Algiers, 5 July 1830'; the dey signed a capitulation promising 'not to infringe on the freedom of people of all classes and their religion' and left for Italy about 10 July. The landing had been at Sidi Ferruch on 14 June. The region is a 30 km radius round Algiers, not the Cliopatria 1830 shape (whose ten Algiers cells run west to 2.03 E and miss the city); the page puts French control at Algiers and nearby coastal points.

region.text: Bône (Annaba)

ledger.note: 1832: the French occupy Bône. The Annaba page: Ottoman rule 'lasted until French occupation in 1832' (no month); the conquest page has Rovigo, appointed at the end of 1831, regaining 'control of Bône and Bougie' that Clauzel had taken and then lost, and Bourmont's 1830 troops withdrawn. The French Algeria page's 1 December 1830 is Rovigo's appointment, not the taking of Bône, and is not used. The Beylik of Constantine page has the province's coast running 'from Béjaïa to Annaba', hence the counterpart; the beylik has no dossier.

region.text: Bougie (Béjaïa)

ledger.note: 1833: Bougie falls. The conquest page: 'in 1833 France captured the city with minimal losses, from Kabyle and Kouloughli forces', after Clauzel had taken and lost it. The defenders were no state with a dossier, so the counterpart is nobody (the Beylik of Constantine page lists Béjaïa among the province's cities, but the conquest page names Kabyle and Kouloughli forces).

region.text: Oran and the coast around Arzew and Mostaganem

ledger.note: 1833: Oran and the coast to Arzew and Mostaganem pass under French control. Voirol 'established French occupation in Oran' and Desmichels 'was given an independent command that gained control over Arzew and Mostaganem'; the page gives no month and does not say who held the towns. No page opened shows the emir (his state dates from 27 November 1832) holding them, so the counterpart is nobody. Cliopatria draws Oran from 1830 and never draws Arzew and Mostaganem before 1842.

region.text: the Sahel and coastal Mitidja cells of the Cliopatria 1834 shape beyond the Algiers radius, Tipaza and Boumerdès provinces

ledger.note: 1834: the annexed 'area of limited occupation near the coast' is wider than the Algiers radius. The conquest page: 'On 22 June 1834, France formally annexed the occupied areas'; the Hadjout were attacked in 1834 and 'crushed by August 1835'. It lists no towns, so the cells are Cliopatria's and the gain bridges a silence. Blida, the Bouira and Kabylia cells of the same shape are not entered: Blida was captured only in 1839 and Kabylia in 1857.

22 July 1834: a royal ordinance organises the occupied territories and is generally treated as the formal annexation of Algeria (the conquest page has 22 June 1834): the occupied coast becomes a colony under a governor-general answerable to the war minister.

region.text: the Oran country of Mascara and Tlemcen

ledger.note: January 1836: the French take Tlemcen. Clauzel occupied Tlemcen and left a garrison, after Mascara, abandoned by Abd al-Qadir, was attacked in December 1835; the Macta defeat of 16 June 1835 had already ended the peace of the Desmichels treaty (26 February 1834, Emirate page).

region.text: the Oran country left to the emir

ledger.note: 30 May 1837: the Treaty of Tafna. Bugeaud and Abd al-Qadir sign; France recognises him as ruler of "about two thirds of Algeria" (the provinces of Oran, Koléa, Médéa, Tlemcen and Algiers named) in return for his recognising French sovereignty, and keeps its ports. The page does not give the place of signing.

region.text: Constantine, captured 13 October 1837

ledger.note: 13 October 1837: Valée storms Constantine. The French Algeria page has Valée capturing Constantine on 13 October 1837 (the conquest page: Damrémont killed in the siege and replaced by Valée; Clauzel repulsed in November 1836). The Beylik of Constantine has no dossier.

region.text: the unoccupied interior: by 1839 the emir controlled more than two-thirds of Algeria, on the French Algeria page

ledger.note: Late 1839: the war resumes. French troops march through the Iron Gates, the defile on the Algiers-Constantine road that Abd al-Qadir claimed under the treaty; he takes it as a breach and renews the jihad (the conquest page adds the Mitidja campaign and the French capture of Blida in 1839). The year is the pages'; the zone is the emirate-of-abdelkader dossier's reading of the emir's ground.

region.text: Blida and its province, the Mitidja foothills

ledger.note: 1839: Blida is captured. The conquest page: the battles of Blida were fought in 1830 'and France was only able to capture Blida in 1839'; the Mitidja campaign of the emir was routed at Oued El Alleug in 1839. The emir held the Algiers hinterland since Tafna (1837), whose provinces the Tafna page names as Oran, Koléa, Médéa, Tlemcen and Algiers.

region.text: Miliana and its province, occupied by Valée's troops

ledger.note: 1840: Miliana is occupied. The Miliana page: Abd al-Qadir 'established a caliphate in Miliana in 1835'; 'The city was occupied in 1840 by Marshal Valée's troops, but the garrison was sieged several times'; 'The town eventually fell under French control in 1842'; the French burned it in 1844. The cells are Cliopatria's 1840 Aïn Defla cells.

region.text: Sétif and the Medjana, the emir's province of Mejdana

ledger.note: 1840: the Sétif country of the Algiers-Constantine belt is held. The conquest page has the policy of 'limited occupation' dropped for 'complete control' in 1840 and the Iron Gates passed in late 1839; the Emirate page's province table lists 'Mejdana (Sétif)' and 'Jibal (Bouïra)' among the emir's eight provinces (no years), so the counterpart is the emirate. The year is the page's, the cells Cliopatria's.

region.text: the Constantine country of the belt (Philippeville, Jijel, Mila, Guelma and the coast to Bône), without Constantine and Bône

ledger.note: 1840: the coast and country around Constantine are held. The Beylik of Constantine page: 'The Beylik collapsed in the 1837 siege of Constantine', so the beylik is not the 1840 counterpart (Ahmed Bey, in the Aurès, 'continued the struggle until he surrendered in 1848'). The conquest page dates the policy change to 1840; the cells are Cliopatria's.

region.text: Mascara and its province, where 'the French establish full control' in 1841

ledger.note: 1841: Mascara comes under full French control. The Mascara page's timeline: '1832: Abd al-Qadir makes Mascara his headquarters', '1835: Mascara is destroyed by the French', '1841: The French establish full control over Mascara'. Cliopatria draws the Mascara cells from 1842.

region.text: the block from Oran south to Tlemcen that the 1842 shape adds to the 1840 belt, without the coast held since 1833 and without Mascara

ledger.note: 1842: Tlemcen and the Oran interior pass to France. The Tlemcen page's timeline has 'France, (French Algeria) 1842-1962' (no month; Clauzel had entered the city in 1836 and the Tafna treaty left it to the emir); the Miliana page has Miliana under French control in 1842 and the conquest page has the emir 'driven into Morocco in 1842'. The year is the pages', the extent of the block Cliopatria's.

region.text: Biskra, from where the Saharan expedition set out

ledger.note: March 1844: the Saharan expedition starts from Biskra under the Duke of Aumale, a 22-year-old general. The page says the expedition began at Biskra, not that Biskra was taken then; the Emirate page lists the Ziban among the emir's eight provinces.

region.text: Oujda and the frontier country around Lalla Maghnia

ledger.note: 19 June 1844: Bugeaud occupies Oujda. The page: Bugeaud violated the frontier and occupied Oujda after border clashes around Lalla Maghnia; the French fleet bombarded Tangier on 6 August and Mogador on 16 August, and Isly was fought on 14 August (the war is the First Franco-Moroccan War).

region.text: the Algerian-Moroccan frontier from the Mediterranean to Teniet el-Sassi

ledger.note: 18 March 1845: the Treaty of Lalla Maghnia fixes the frontier from the Mediterranean to Teniet el-Sassi, some seventy miles inland (after the Treaty of Tangier of 10 September 1844, in which Morocco recognised Algeria as part of the French Empire and outlawed Abd al-Qadir): Yich and Figuig to Morocco; Aïn Séfra, Sfissifa, Asla, Tiout, Chellala, El Bayadh and Boussemghoun to Algeria; the desert south of Figuig left undelimited.

region.text: the Tell, the High Plateaux and the east that the 1846 shape adds to the 1842 shape, without Biskra, Kabylia, Bouira and the two cells in modern Tunisia

ledger.note: 1846: the French row jumps from 48,573 to 211,876 km2. The conquest page dates only steps: the Kabylia campaign of 1845, the ambush at Issers and the surrender of Ahmed bin Salem in 1846 (which the page says ended Abd al-Qadir's influence in the east), the smala raid of 1843 and Biskra in March 1844; it gives no extent of French control in 1846. Cliopatria's single step is entered as bridging; the 1847 surrender ends the fighting. Not entered: Kabylia and Bouira province (the Kabylia page has Kabylia conquered in 1857; the Battle of Tizi Ouzou of 1845 and the Issers ambush of 1846 are at its edge) and Laghouat (the Laghouat page: siege of 21 November-4 December 1852). The Médéa page gives no French date for Médéa; the extent of the gain remains the page's silence.

region.text: the unoccupied interior, the emir's ground to the end

ledger.note: 23 December 1847: Abd al-Qadir surrenders. The Emirate page's infobox gives 23 December 1847; the French Algeria page has him surrendering at the end of 1847 to General Lamoricière on a promise of safe passage to Egypt or Palestine, and then held at Château d'Amboise.

region.text: Algeria, from 1848 three departments of France

ledger.note: End of 1847: the conquest is complete and the colony passes into France. The French Algeria page runs 'French colony (1830-1848)' then 'part of France (1848-1962)': the Second Republic's constitution of 1848 declared Algeria an integral part of France with three civil departments (Alger, Oran, Constantine). Cliopatria closes this row in 1847 and draws Algeria in its French Africa row from 1848.

wars.name: Invasion of Algiers in 1830

zones.text: Algiers and the Sidi Ferruch landing coast

wars.outcome: About 34,000 French troops land at Sidi Ferruch on 14 June 1830, win at Staouéli on 19 June and enter Algiers on 5 July; the dey capitulates and leaves for Italy.
wars.note: The campaign has its own article (linked from the French Algeria page) which was not opened; dates are the French Algeria page's. The Regency dossier covers the Algerian side.

wars.name: French conquest of Algeria

zones.text: the Oran country of Mascara and Tlemcen, 1836-1837

wars.outcome: France annexes the occupied coast in 1834, signs the Treaty of Tafna in 1837, storms Constantine in 1837, resumes the war in late 1839, takes the emir's smala in 1843, defeats Morocco in 1844 and forces Abd al-Qadir's surrender on 23 December 1847.
wars.note: Named engagements on the pages: Macta (16 June 1835, an Abd al-Qadir victory), Sikkak (6 July 1836, a Bugeaud victory), Oued El Alleug (1839), the smala (1843), Sidi-Brahim (1845, a French force destroyed), Issers (1846). The emirate's contests with France are the ledger's 1836-1837 and 1839-1847 pairs; the 1830-1835 fighting around Oran and Bône took no ground that the pages date.

wars.name: Siege of Constantine (1837)
wars.outcome: Clauzel's column is repulsed in November 1836; Damrémont is killed in the 1837 siege and Valée storms the city on 13 October 1837.
wars.note: No contest span is entered: the 1836 column took no ground, and the city changes hands at once in 1837.

wars.name: First Franco-Moroccan War

zones.text: Oujda and the frontier around Lalla Maghnia

wars.outcome: French victory: Oujda occupied 19 June 1844, Tangier bombarded 6 August, Isly won 14 August, Mogador taken 16 August; the Treaty of Tangier (10 September 1844) ends the war and the Treaty of Lalla Maghnia (18 March 1845) sets the frontier from the sea to Teniet el-Sassi.
wars.note: Morocco's dossier has the matching contest events.

certainty.note: French control is coast, towns and columns' reach: the 1830-1836 "limited occupation" is a string of garrisoned places and the interior was the emir's or Constantine's. No line rests on a treaty (the Tafna treaty of 1837 names provinces, not lines). Kabylia and the Bouira uplands were outside French control throughout (Kabylia fully conquered in 1857).

The frontier with Morocco is sharp from 18 March 1845 (the Treaty of Lalla Maghnia, from the Mediterranean to Teniet el-Sassi); south of Figuig it was left undelimited, the Saharan edge and the frontier with Tunis were undefined, and Kabylia remained outside French government.

sources.title: French Algeria
sources.note: Infobox (5 July 1830; capital Algiers; 585,814 km2 in 1899), the 1830-1848 timeline, Bône 1 December 1830, annexation 22 July 1834, Constantine 13 October 1837, the 1848 constitution; Treaty of Desmichels and Lalla Maghnia not on the page.

sources.title: French conquest of Algeria
sources.note: Extent of French control by stage; Bougie, Oran, Arzew, Mostaganem 1833; Tlemcen January 1836; Tafna May 1837; the Iron Gates late 1839; 1840 policy shift; the smala 1843; Biskra March 1844; Kabylia 1845-1846; surrender December 1847. Gives no month for Constantine and no Isly or Lalla Maghnia. Reopened for the repair: Bône and Bougie under Rovigo, Blida 1839, Larbaa February 1837, Hadjout 1834-1835, the 22 June 1834 annexation.

sources.title: Treaty of Tafna
sources.note: Signed 30 May 1837 by Bugeaud and Abd al-Qadir, about two-thirds of Algeria and five provinces named for the emir; breakdown in late 1839 over the Iron Gates.

sources.title: First Franco-Moroccan War
sources.note: Oujda 19 June 1844, Tangier 6 August, Isly 14 August, Mogador 16 August, Treaty of Tangier 10 September 1844, Treaty of Lalla Maghnia 18 March 1845 and the frontier it set.

sources.title: Emirate of Abdelkader
sources.note: Thin: infobox dates (established 27 November 1832, Desmichels 26 February 1834, Tafna 30 May 1837, surrender 23 December 1847) and the list of eight provinces including the Ziban; no year-by-year territory. Also the province table (Titteri, Miliana, Tlemcen, Mascara, Sahara, Mejdana, Ziban, Jibal), no years.

sources.title: Beylik of Constantine
sources.note: Province coast from Béjaïa to Annaba; collapsed in the 1837 siege of Constantine; Ahmed Bey in the Aurès until 1848.

sources.title: Kabylia
sources.note: Kabylia 'fully and entirely conquered and subdued by France' in 1857 (Battle of Icheriden).

sources.title: Tlemcen
sources.note: Timeline: French Algeria 1842-1962; Clauzel entered the city in 1836.

sources.title: Laghouat
sources.note: French punitive campaign and siege of Laghouat, 21 November-4 December 1852; no earlier French rule.

sources.title: Médéa
sources.note: Capital of the emir's part after Tafna (1837); no French date.

sources.title: Miliana
sources.note: Emir's caliphate from 1835; occupied by Valée's troops in 1840; under French control in 1842; burned 1844.

sources.title: Mascara, Algeria
sources.note: Timeline: emir's headquarters 1832; destroyed by the French 1835; full French control 1841.

notes:
FRENCH ALGERIA (Cliopatria row 1830-1847, 5 shapes). Five pages opened (the budget): French Algeria, French conquest of Algeria, Treaty of Tafna, First Franco-Moroccan War, Emirate of Abdelkader (thin).

END YEAR. The French Algeria page runs the colony 1830-1848 and 'part of France' 1848-1962. Cliopatria ends this row in 1847 and its French Africa row (1846-1957, other group) takes Algeria in 1848 (799 cells); the dossier ends in 1847 and hands the land to french-africa. Algeria from 1848 to 1962 is french-africa's and, for 1958-1962, the French Fifth Republic row whose shape still contains Algeria (data/README.md).

CORRECTIONS ENTERED (from pages): Bougie, Arzew and Mostaganem join in 1833, not 1834 or 1842 (conquest page); Constantine falls on 13 October 1837, not 1840 (French Algeria page); Biskra is the base of the Saharan expedition in March 1844, not 1846 (conquest page); the colony's formal annexation is 22 July 1834 (French Algeria page; the conquest page says 22 June).

NOT SETTLED.
